the development of a Web-based preparatory educational intervention for patients with cancer.
the development of a preparatory Web-based educational intervention to support patients with cancer before consultations with their physician.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mode-tailoring intervention did not yield any significant differences on the patient outcomes in the older patient group.
mode tailoring is not a necessary condition to improve patient outcomes.
the mode-tailoring of online preparatory information is a promising strategy to improve information processing and communication outcomes in newly diagnosed younger and older patients with cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
offering patients preparatory online information in a mode-tailed manner is beneficial for younger and older patients with cancer.
offering preparatory online information to patients with cancer before consultations benefits patient outcomes, including knowledge and anxiety.
the mode-tailoring of information to patients with cancer, especially younger patients, is beneficial.
The main takeaway from our work is that
offering online information before consultations can be a valuable tool to improve the communication between health care professionals and patients with cancer, regardless of age.
